items.item_text: resume
cover letter

High school diploma or equivalent and three years of laboratory experience; or two years of college including coursework in the natural, physical, or biological sciences and two years of laboratory experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Previous experience working in a biological research laboratory.

Under general supervision, the Lab Assistant 3 provides skilled technical and operational support for research in the Doudna laboratory. This position performs standardized, recurring molecular biology, microbiology, protein, and nucleic acid procedures using established protocols; prepares reagents and samples; maintains laboratory materials and records; and operates routine laboratory equipment. The Lab Assistant 3 organizes technical data for review by research staff and may assist with basic computer-based sequence processing and data organization using established workflows. This position works closely with research personnel to support reliable and reproducible laboratory research activities. Additionally, this position provides technical research support for projects investigating the molecular mechanisms of novel CRISPR-Cas and related microbial defense systems, contributing to the characterization of candidate defense systems identified through genomic and bioinformatic analyses. Under the guidance of the postdoctoral scholar and the principal investigator, the Lab Assistant 3 may also assist with basic computational analysis, including genome mining, sequence analysis, data organization and visualization, and in silico protein structure prediction using tools such as AlphaFold2/ColabFold.
Molecular Biology and Reagent Preparation - 30%

Performs standardized and recurring molecular biology procedures in support of laboratory research, including PCR, DNA assembly using established methods, bacterial transformation, plasmid preparation, restriction digestion, agarose gel electrophoresis, and nucleic acid purification.
Prepares, labels, stores, and tracks DNA constructs, reagents, and samples according to established laboratory procedures.
Maintains accurate records of materials and procedures performed.
Recombinant Protein and Sample Preparation - 20%

Performs established procedures for bacterial culture, recombinant protein expression, cell harvesting and lysis, affinity purification, size-exclusion chromatography, and related sample-processing steps.
Prepares buffers and other materials, operates routine laboratory equipment, records purification outputs and protein concentration measurements, and prepares samples for use by research personnel.
RNA and Nucleic Acid Technical Procedures - 20%

Prepares RNA and DNA substrates and performs established procedures including in vitro transcription, nucleic acid purification, native and denaturing polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis, and standardized nucleic-acid assay procedures.
Records experimental conditions and organizes resulting data for review by supervising researchers.
Laboratory Operations, Materials, and Documentation - 20%

Prepares commonly used buffers, media, solutions, and reagents; organizes and maintains laboratory samples and shared materials; assists with inventory, ordering, receiving, labeling, and storage of laboratory supplies; maintains work areas and equipment; and follows established biological, chemical, and waste-disposal procedures.
Technical Data and Computational Support - 10%
Records, organizes, and performs routine processing of laboratory and sequence-based data using established software and workflows.
Prepares basic tables, graphs, sample records, and sequence files for review by research personnel.
May run established sequence-processing or computational workflows using inputs and parameters provided by supervising researchers.
Familiarity with recombinant protein purification, RNA handling, polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis, or related laboratory procedures.
Additional college coursework in biology, biochemistry, microbiology, molecular biology, chemistry, or a related discipline (Preferred).

Working knowledge of standard molecular biology and biochemical laboratory techniques sufficient to perform established procedures, including pipetting, solution preparation, bacterial culture, PCR, nucleic acid purification, and gel electrophoresis.
Working knowledge of laboratory procedures for preparation and handling of biological samples, reagents, buffers, and other research materials.
Ability to accurately follow detailed written and oral laboratory protocols and standard operating procedures.
Ability to maintain complete and accurate laboratory records, sample inventories, reagent records, and documentation of procedures performed.
Ability to recognize deviations from expected technical performance, verify routine procedural steps and controls, and communicate unresolved problems to supervising research personnel.
Ability to organize multiple samples and recurring laboratory tasks, manage priorities, and perform technical work accurately and reproducibly.
Ability to operate and maintain routine laboratory equipment according to established procedures and manufacturer instructions.
Ability to work independently on assigned standardized procedures and collaboratively with laboratory personnel.
Knowledge of laboratory safety practices and ability to follow institutional procedures for biological materials, chemicals, equipment, and waste disposal.
